findings.title: SET-to-ZSET change breaks in-flight segment keys on deploy
findings.body: Segment buffers are now written with ZADD and read with ZCARD, ZUNIONSTORE, and ZSCAN (add-buffer.lua and _load_segment_data). The previous release stored the same span-buf:s:* keys as Redis SETs (SADD/SUNIONSTORE/SSCAN). There is no new key prefix, dual-read, or WRONGTYPE handling. On a rolling deploy, keys still held as SETs (redis_ttl defaults to 3600s) make ZADD and ZSCAN raise WRONGTYPE; one such error fails the whole non-transactional pipeline, so both insert and flush abort for any batch that touches an old key. Old processes still running set commands fail the same way on keys the new code has already converted to sorted sets. Segments that cannot be flushed remain until TTL and are then dropped, so in-flight spans are lost and the consumer retries until those keys expire.

findings.title: Insert-time eviction ignores max_segment_spans and drops spans silently
findings.body: When a segment has more than 1000 members the Lua script ZPOPMINs it down to 1000. That limit is hardcoded and is not SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans (default 1001, and a constructor argument callers can change). The flush-time backstop that skipped segments with more than max_segment_spans, logged an error, and incremented spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded was removed from _load_segment_data. A segment of 1001 spans, which the default config previously flushed intact, now loses a span with no metric, log, or truncation flag on the flushed payload. Changing max_segment_spans has no effect. The cap also only runs inside the script, which is a separate pipeline from the earlier ZADD; if the script errors after that ZADD, nothing else enforces a span count before the flusher loads and produces the segment. ZPOPMIN keeps the highest end_timestamp_precise scores, so a root span that does not have the latest end time can be deleted while the has-root-span flag stays set and the segment is still flushed on the shorter root timeout, missing its root payload.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE sums timestamp scores and evicts the wrong spans
findings.body: Both ZUNIONSTORE calls (the span-key merge and the parent-key merge) omit AGGREGATE, so Redis uses SUM. Member scores are end_timestamp_precise values, and ZPOPMIN later drops the lowest scores to enforce the cap. If the same payload is in both inputs — a retry after a partial write, or the same span stored under its own id and under the parent id — the scores are added, roughly doubling the timestamp. Those members then sort as newer than spans with a real later end time, so once the segment is over the cap the script keeps the corrupted members and drops newly ingested spans. The union needs AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN) so each member keeps an actual timestamp.

findings.title: Optimized audit-log pagination crashes on datetime ordering
findings.body: When optimized_pagination=true and the caller is a superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access, the audit log endpoint paginates AuditLogEntry with OptimizedCursorPaginator and order_by=-datetime. That paginator's get_item_key runs math.floor/math.ceil on the raw field, which is a datetime, so build_cursor raises TypeError as soon as a page contains any rows. value_from_cursor also returns the raw cursor number instead of converting it back to a datetime the way DateTimePaginator does, so a following page would compare the datetime column to an integer. The new path therefore 500s for every organization that has audit log rows. enable_advanced_features is passed into Endpoint.paginate, which this PR does not change; if that method does not forward unknown kwargs, the request fails even earlier with TypeError. There is no test for this path. The default DateTimePaginator branch is unchanged, but the new branch is unusable.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets are applied to audit-log queryset slices
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator, when enable_advanced_features is set, takes the client-supplied cursor offset and, if it is negative, slices the queryset from that negative start. OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint turns the flag on for any superuser or member with has_global_access who passes optimized_pagination=true. The comments say this is meant to read past normal pagination bounds and that queryset permission checks make it safe. Those filters only choose which rows are in the queryset; they do not validate the offset. OffsetPaginator rejects a negative offset with BadPaginationError; this path does not. Django QuerySet raises ValueError on a negative slice, so the current effect is an unhandled 500 rather than extra rows, but the bound check was removed on purpose on an audit-log API and a crafted cursor reaches the ORM. Negative offsets must be rejected before slicing. The same idea was added to BasePaginator.get_result, which now keeps a negative offset for previous-page cursors and comments that the queryset will handle it; it will not, and that helper is shared by every cursor-paginated endpoint. This is unrelated to the span-buffer change and should not be merged.

findings.title: Redirect walk cap cut from 10000 to 1000 without a failure signal
findings.body: The loop that follows span-buf:sr redirects to find the segment key was reduced from 10000 iterations to 1000, and the comment that this cap can fail to join a deep chain was removed. If the chain is longer than 1000, the script stops on an intermediate span id, records the new span's redirect to that intermediate node, and merges into the wrong buffer. Flush then emits a split or mis-joined trace and nothing increments a metric when the cap is hit. Typical traces are shallower than this, but the old limit was intentional and the new one fails closed only by silently attaching spans to the wrong segment.

findings.title: No test covers eviction, score order, or the ZSET migration
findings.body: The buffer tests only add end_timestamp_precise to existing fixtures of four or five spans that all use the timestamp 1700000000.0. Nothing builds a segment larger than 1000 spans, asserts that the lowest scores are the ones removed, checks that max_segment_spans is the cap that is actually applied, or merges two sorted sets that share a member and checks the resulting score. Insert-time eviction, wrong-span drops from summed scores, and ZSCAN of sorted-set segment keys can all regress without a failing test. The new audit-log paginator path is also untested.

findings.title: Glossary still calls segment keys sets that hold every span
findings.body: The SpansBuffer glossary still describes span-buf:s:* as set keys that contain all span payloads for a segment, and the insert steps above still say the payload is added to a set. Those keys are now sorted sets scored by end_timestamp_precise, and members over the cap are deleted during insert, so a flushed segment may already be missing spans. Operators following this text will run SCARD or SSCAN, which fail with WRONGTYPE on the new keys, and will not know truncation is expected.
